sections.title: Design Examples: Geotechnical Ultimate Limit States for Static Analysis
sections.body:
[p. 294] Design examples provided in this appendix are described below. Settlement calculations for these same design examples are provided in Appendix C. No examples for uplift or global stability are presented in this appendix. Refer to EM 1110-2-2100 and EM 1110-2-1902, respectively.

Example B-1 Undrained vertical bearing capacity for isolated footing on clay.
Example B-2 Undrained vertical bearing capacity for continuous footing on clay.
Example B-3 Drained vertical bearing capacity for isolated footing on sand with water table below the shear zone. Dense over soft condition and shear within upper layer.
a. Solution for drained bearing capacity analysis, shear within surface layer.
b. Solution for undrained punch-through analysis.
Example B-4 Undrained vertical bearing capacity for isolated basement footing on clay, influence of construction dewatering.
a. Solution for the end-of-construction case (dewatered condition).
b. Solution for the long-term water level case (pre-construction water level re-established).
Example B-5 Undrained vertical bearing capacity for isolated footing on clay.
a. Solution for the analysis of bearing capacity based on undrained strength.
b. Solution for the bearing capacity analysis based on the pressuremeter.
c. Solution for punch-through analysis based on undrained strength.
d. Average safety factor from multiple methods.
Example B-6 Drained vertical bearing capacity for isolated footing on sand with water table in the shear zone, as compared to undrained punch-through failure into soft clay.
a. Solution for drained bearing capacity analysis within surface layer.
b. Solution for undrained punch-through analysis.
Example B-7 Drained vertical bearing capacity for isolated footing on sand, comparison of soil parameters and in situ tests.
a. Solution for drained bearing capacity analysis within surface layer.
b. Solution for the analysis based on in situ tests (PMT, CPT, SPT).

sections.title: Given
sections.body:
[p. 295] Given: A 7.0-ft by 7.0-ft isolated footing supporting a 40-kip column load bearing 2.0 ft below grade on the clay profile illustrated in Figure B-1. A summary of calculations is presented in Table B-1b. Correction factors for the USACE and AASHTO methods are presented In the calculations. Section 5-5f recommends performing analyses with both methods and average the results when assessing the safety factor.

Figure B-1. Foundation and soil conditions for Example B-1

[p. 296] Table B-1a Solution for undrained bearing capacity analysis (isolated footing)
Step 1 | Collect geometric information for the problem and input to Table B-1b. There is no eccentricity (e = 0), so footing geometry is equal to effective footing geometry (see paragraph 5-4a).
Footing width, B = B′ = 7 ft (Row 1)
Footing length, L = L′ = 7 ft (Row 2)
Footing effective area, A′ = B′ × L′ = 7 ft = 49 ft^2 (Row 3)
[Note (not printed): Table B-1a, Step 1 (p. 296): the print writes A′ = B′ × L′ = 7 ft = 49 ft^2; the product is 7 ft × 7 ft = 49 ft^2 (the first factor is not printed). The line above is as printed.]
Embedment depth of the footing, Df = 2 ft (Row 4)
Unit wt. between base of the footing and ground surface, γ = 0.120 kcf (Row 5)
Step 2 | For undrained analysis use Eq. 5-22 for qult and correction factors in Table 5-4.
Step 3 | For undrained analysis with φ = 0, Nγ is zero. Cohesion c is taken as the undrained strength su. Eq. 5-22 simplifies to qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq. Since Nq = 1 for φ = 0, and all undrained correction factors are 1 (Table 5-4), Eq. 5-29 further simplifies to:
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0
The total stress at the base of the footing is:
qo = γ · Df = 0.120 kcf · 2 ft = 0.24 ksf (Row 6)
The shear zone is typically taken as 1/2 the footing width, or 3.5 ft. The bottom of the shear zone is estimated as Df + 0.5B = 5.5 ft. If the soil in Layer 2 (10 ft to 25 ft) is weaker than soil in Layer 1 (0 ft to 10 ft), a deeper shear zone will need to be checked. The Layer 2 soil is stronger, so strength of Layer 1 soil is used for analysis.
c = su = 500 psf = 0.5 ksf (Row 7)
The cohesion bearing capacity factor Nc = 2 + π = 5.14 (Row 8)
The undrained shape factor for both the USACE and FHWA methods is (Table 5-4):
sc = 1 + 0.2 (B′/L′) = 1 + 0.2((7 ft)/(7 ft)) = 1.2 (Row 9)
The undrained depth factor for the USACE methods is (Table 5-4):
dc = 1 + 0.2 (Df/B′) ≤ 1.5 = 1 + 0.2((2 ft)/(7 ft)) = 1.06 (Row 10)
The FHWA method does not explicitly include a depth for undrained analysis, so dc = 1. For this example, there is no load inclination, no base inclination, and no ground inclination.
ic = 1 (Row 11)
bc = 1 (Row 12)
gc = 1 (Row 13)
Step 4a | For the USACE method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 14.
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult = 1.2 · 1.06 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.5 ksf · 5.14 + 0.24 ksf
qult = 3.27 ksf + 0.24 ksf = 3.51 ksf
[p. 297]
Step 4b | For the FHWA method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 14.
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult = 1.2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.5 ksf · 5.14 + 0.24 ksf
qult = 3.08 ksf + 0.24 ksf = 3.32 ksf
Step 5 | The load on the soil is a combination of the column load and foundation weight and is expressed as a stress based on the effective area (Eq. 5-13).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′
Column load, Q = 40 kips (Row 15)
Unit weight of concrete, γconc = 0.150 kcf
Weight of foundation, Wf = A · Df · γconc = 49 ft^2 · 2 ft · 0.15 kcf = 14.7 kips (Row 16)
Gross equivalent bearing pressure, (Eq. 5-13) (Row 17).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′ = (40 kips + 14.7 kips)/(49 ft^2) = 1.12 ksf
Step 6a | The minimum factor of safety for ultimate bearing capacity is 3 (Chapter 2). For the USACE method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (3.51 ksf)/(1.12 ksf) = 3.1 ≥ 3 OK ü
Step 6b | For the FHWA method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (3.32 ksf)/(1.12 ksf) = 3.0 ≥ 3 OK ü

For this case, there was a weaker layer above a stronger layer, so the bearing capacity in the weak layer controls resistance. sections.body:
[p. 298] Given: In addition to constructing the 7.0-ft by 7.0-ft isolated footing in Example B-1, a 2-ft-wide continuous footing with a loading of 1.2 kips/foot is to be constructed adjacent to the isolated footing as illustrated in Figure B-2. Both footings are to bear 2 ft below existing grade.

[p. 299] Figure B-2. Foundation and soil conditions for Example B-2

Table B-2a Solution for undrained bearing capacity analysis (continuous footing)
Step 1 | Collect geometric information for the problem and input to Table B-2b. There is no eccentricity (e = 0), so footing geometry is equal to effective footing geometry (see paragraph 5-4a).
Footing width, B = B′ = 2 ft (Row 1)
For continuous footings, loads are considered per-unit length, and length is not specifically included in analysis; length L= L = L′ = not applica le (Row 2)
Footing effective area, A′ = B′ · L′ = 2 ft · 1 ft = 2 ft^2/ft (Row 3)
Embedment depth of the footing, Df = 2 ft (Row 4)
Unit wt. between base of the footing and ground surface, γ = 0.120 kcf (Row 5)
Step 2 | Use Eq. 5-28 for undrained qult and correction factors in Table 5-4.
[p. 300]
Step 3 | For undrained analysis with φ = 0, Nγ is zero. The value of cohesion c is taken as the undrained strength su. Eq. 5-22 simplifies to qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq. Since Nq = 1 for φ = 0, and all undrained correction factors are 1 (Table 5-4), Eq. 5-29 further simplifies to qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
The total stress at the base of the footing is:
qo = γ · Df = 0.120 kcf · 2 ft = 0.24 ksf (Row 6)
The shear zone is typically taken as 1 footing width, or 2 ft. The bottom of the shear zone estimated as Df + B = 4 ft. The estimated shear zone is within Layer 1 (0 ft to 10 ft), so strength of Layer 1 soil is used for analysis.
c = su = 500 psf = 0.5 ksf (Row 7)
The cohesion bearing capacity factor, Nc = 2 + π = 5.14 (Row 8)
The undrained shape factor for a continuous footing for both the USACE and FHWA methods is 1 (Row 9).
The undrained depth factor for the USACE method is (Table 5-4):
dc = 1 + 0.2 (Df/B′) ≤ 1.5 = 1 + 0.2((2 ft)/(2 ft)) = 1.2 (Row 10)
The FHWA method does not explicitly include a depth for undrained analysis, so dc = 1. For this example, there is no load inclination, no base inclination, and no ground inclination.
ic = 1 (Row 11)
bc = 1 (Row 12)
gc = 1 (Row 13)
Step 4a | For the USACE method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 14.
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult = 1 · 1.2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.5 ksf · 5.14 + 0.24 ksf
qult = 3.08 ksf + 0.24 ksf = 3.32 ksf
Step 4b | For the FHWA method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 14.
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult = 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.5 ksf · 5.14 + 0.24 ksf
qult = 2.57 ksf + 0.24 ksf = 2.81 ksf
[p. 301]
Step 5 | The load on the soil is a combination of the column load and foundation weight and is expressed as a stress based on the effective area (Eq. 5-13).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′
Column load, Q = 1.2 kips/ft (Row 15)
Unit weight of concrete, γconc = 0.150 kcf
Weight of foundation, Wf = A · Df · γconc = 2 ft^2/ft · 2 ft · 0.15 kcf = 0.6 kips/ft (Row 16)
Gross equivalent bearing pressure, (Eq. 5-13).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′ = (1.2 kips/ft + 0.6 kips/ft)/(2 ft^2/ft) = 0.9 ksf (Row 17)
Step 6a | The minimum factor of safety for ultimate bearing capacity is 3 (Chapter 2). For the USACE method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (3.32 ksf)/(0.9 ksf) = 3.7 ≥ 3 OK ü
Step 6b | For the FHWA method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (2.81 ksf)/(0.9 ksf) = 3.1 ≥ 3 OK ü

sections.title: Given
sections.body:
[p. 302] Given: Prior to constructing the footings, site grades are raised by placing 8 ft of areal fill throughout the entire site, including beneath the building (see Figure B-3). The fill material placed beneath the building and 10 ft beyond the building limits consists of approved structural fill material. A 7.0-ft by 7.0-ft isolated footing supporting a 90-kip column load will bear 2 ft below the new site grade.

[p. 303] Figure B-3. Foundation and soil conditions for Example B-3

Table B-3a Solution for drained bearing capacity analysis, shear within surface layer
Step 1 | Collect geometric information for the problem and input to Table B-3c. There is no eccentricity (e = 0), so footing geometry is equal to effective footing geometry (see paragraph 5-4a).
Footing width, B = B′ = 7 ft (Row 1)
Footing length, L = L′ = 7 ft (Row 2)
Footing effective area, A′ = B′ · L′ = 7 ft · 7 ft = 49 ft^2 (Row 3)
Embedment depth of the footing, Df = 2 ft (Row 4)
Depth of water table, Dw = 13 ft (Row 5)
Unit wt. between base of the footing and ground surface, γ = 0.135 kcf (Row 6)
[p. 304]
Step 2 | Identify that the problem involves free-draining soils (sands, silty sands, and non-plastic silts) in the layer immediately below the footing, and that the bearing capacity limit state must be assessed for drained conditions (Table 5-1). Use Eq. 5-22 for qult and correction factors in Table 5-2 and Table 5-3.
Step 3 | For drained analysis with cohesion c = 0, Eq. 5-22 simplifies to:
qult = sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq + sγ · dγ · iγ · bγ · gγ · 1/2 · B′ · γ′ · Nγ
The ratio of the effective unit weight in the shear zone to the total unit weight differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, (Eq. 5-19) (Row 7):
γ′/γ ≈ [0.45 + 0.55 ((max(DW − Df, 0))/B)] ≤ 1
γ′/γ ≈ [0.45 + 0.55 ((max(13 ft − 2 ft, 0))/(7 ft))] ≤ 1 = 1
For FHWA, (Eq. 5-20) (Row 7):
γ′/γ ≈ CWγ = [0.5 + 0.5 (DW/(1.5B + Df))] ≤ 1
γ′/γ ≈ CWγ = [0.5 + 0.5 ((13 ft)/(1.5(7 ft) + 2 ft))] ≤ 1 = 1
The effective stress at the base of the footing is:
qo = γm · Df − uo = 0.135 kcf · 2 ft − 0 ksf = 0.27 ksf (Row 8)
The shear zone is typically taken as 1 footing width, or 7 ft. The bottom of the shear zone estimated as Df + B = 9 ft. The estimated shear zone is within Layer 1 (0 ft to 10 ft), so strength of Layer 1 soil is used for analysis. Punch-through failure into the underlying weak layer will be checked in a separate analysis.
φ′ = 34° (Row 9)
The flow number, or principal stress ratio is (Table 5-2) (Row 10):
N = (1 + sinφ′)/(1 − sinφ′) = (1 + sin(34°))/(1 − sin(34°)) = 1.56/0.44 = 3.54
[p. 305]
Step 4 | The dimensionless bearing capacity for surcharge is (Table 5-2) (Row 11):
Nq = N · e^(π·tanφ′) = 3.54e^(π·tan(34°)) = 3.54e^2.12 = 3.54 · 8.32 = 29.46
The drained shape factor for surcharge differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, (Table 5-2) (Row 12):
sq = 1 + 0.1N(B′/L′) = 1 + 0.1 · 3.54 ((7 ft)/(7 ft)) = 1.35
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 12):
sq = 1 + (B′/L′) tanφ = 1 + ((7 ft)/(7 ft)) tan(34°) = 1 + (1 · 0.67) = 1.67
The drained depth factor for surcharge differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, (Table 5-2) (Row 13):
dq = 1 + 0.1√N(Df/B′) = 1 + 0.1√3.54 ((2 ft)/(7 ft)) = 1 + 0.1 · 1.88 · 0.29 = 1.05
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 13):
dq = 1 + 2tanφ′ · (1 − sinφ′)^2 · atan(Df/B′)
dq = 1 + 2tan(34°) · (1 − sin(34°))^2 · atan((2 ft)/(7 ft))
dq = 1 + 2 · 0.67 · (1 − 0.56)^2 · 0.28 = 1.07
For this example, there is no load inclination, no base inclination, and no ground inclination.
ic = 1 (Row 14)
bc = 1 (Row 15)
gc = 1 (Row 16)
[p. 306]
Step 5 | The dimensionless bearing capacity for soil effective weight differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, (Table 5-2) (Row 17):
Nγ = (Nq − 1) · tan(1.4φ′) = (29.46 − 1) · tan(1.4 · 34°)
Nγ = 28.46 · tan(47.6°) = 28.46 · 1.095 = 31.17
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 17):
Nγ = 2(Nq + 1) · tan(φ′) = 2 · (29.46 + 1) · tan(34°)
Nγ = 60.92 · 0.675 = 41.09
The drained shape factor for soil effective weight differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, the shape factors for surcharge and soil effective weight are the same (Table 5-2) (Row 18):
sγ = 1 + 0.1N(B′/L′) = 1 + 0.1 · 3.54 ((7 ft)/(7 ft)) = 1.35
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 18):
sγ = 1 − 0.4 (B′/L′) = 1 − 0.4 ((7 ft)/(7 ft)) = 1 − 0.4 = 0.6
The drained depth factor for surcharge soil effective weight differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, the shape factors for surcharge and soil effective weight are the same (Table 5-2) (Row 19):
dγ = 1 + 0.1√N(Df/B′) = 1 + 0.1√3.54 ((2 ft)/(7 ft)) = 1 + 0.1 · 1.88 · 0.29 = 1.05
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 19): dγ = 1
For this example, there is no load inclination, no base inclination, and no ground inclination.
ic = 1 (Row 20)
bc = 1 (Row 21)
gc = 1 (Row 22)
Step 6a | For the USACE method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 23 as:
qult = sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq + sγ · dγ · iγ · bγ · gγ · 1/2 · B′ · γ′ · Nγ
qult = 1.35 · 1.05 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.27 ksf · 29.46 + 1.35 · 1.05 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1/2 · 7 ft · 0.135 kcf · 31.17
qult = 11.27 ksf + 20.88 ksf = 32.15 ksf
Step 6b | For the FHWA method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 23 as:
qult = sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq + sγ · dγ · iγ · bγ · gγ · 1/2 · B′ · γ′ · Nγ
qult = 1.67 · 1.07 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.27 ksf · 29.46 + 0.6 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1/2 · 7 ft · 0.135 kcf · 41.09
qult = 14.21 ksf + 11.65 ksf = 25.86 ksf
[p. 307]
Step 7 | The load on the soil is a combination of the column load and foundation weight and is expressed as a stress based on the effective area (Eq. 5-13).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′
Column load, Q = 90 kips (Row 24)
Unit weight of concrete, γconc = 0.150 kcf
Weight of foundation, Wf = A · Df · γconc = 49 ft^2 · 2 ft · 0.15 kcf = 14.7 kips (Row 25)
Gross equivalent bearing pressure, (Eq. 5-13) (Row 26).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′ = (90 kips + 14.7 kips)/(49 ft^2) = 2.14 ksf
Step 8a | The minimum factor of safety for ultimate bearing capacity is 3 (Chapter 2). For the USACE method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23) (Row 27).
FS = qult/qeq = (32.15 ksf)/(2.14 ksf) = 15 ≥ 3 OK ü
Step 8b | For the FHWA method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23) (Row 27).
FS = qult/qeq = (25.86 ksf)/(2.14 ksf) = 12.1 ≥ 3 OK ü

Table B-3b Solution for undrained punch-through analysis
Step 1 | Collect geometric information for the problem. There is no eccentricity (e = 0), so footing geometry is equal to effective footing geometry (see paragraph 5-4a). The geometry information is the same as that for the drained analysis of Layer 1.
Footing width, B = B′ = 7 ft (Row 1)
Footing length, L = L′ = 7 ft (Row 2)
Footing effective area, A′ = B′ · L′ = 7 ft · 7 ft = 49 ft^2 (Row 3)
Embedment depth of the footing, Df = 2 ft (Row 4)
Depth of water table, Dw = 13 ft (Row 5)
Unit wt. between base of the footing and ground surface, γ = 0.135 kcf (Row 6)
Step 2 | Identify that the problem of punch-through into the underlying soil involves low permeability soils (clayey soils and plastic silts), and that the bearing capacity limit state must be assessed for undrained conditions (Table 5-1). Use Eq. 5-22 for qult and correction factors in Table 5-4.
[p. 308]
Step 3 | For undrained analysis with φ = 0, Nγ is zero. The value of cohesion, c, is taken as the undrained strength su. Eq. 5-22 simplifies to:
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq
Since Nq = 1 for φ = 0, and all undrained correction factors are 1 (Table 5-4), Eq. 5-29 further simplifies to: qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
The total stress at the base of the footing is:
qo = γ · Df = 0.135 kcf · 2 ft = 0.27 ksf (Row 8)
The shear zone is typically taken as 1 footing width, or 7 ft, but may extend to approximately 2 footings widths when softer soils are at depth. The weaker soils in Layer 2 soil are used for the punch-through analysis.
c = su = 500 psf = 0.5 ksf (Row 9)
The cohesion bearing capacity factor, Nc = 2 + π = 5.14 (Row 10)
The undrained shape factor for both the USACE and FHWA methods is (Table 5-4):
sc = 1 + 0.2 (B′/L′) = 1 + 0.2((7 ft)/(7 ft)) = 1.2 (Row 11)
The undrained depth factor for the USACE methods is (Table 5-4):
dc = 1 + 0.2 (Df/B′) ≤ 1.5 = 1 + 0.2 ((2 ft)/(7 ft)) = 1.06 (Row 12)
The FHWA method does not explicitly include a depth for undrained analysis, so dc = 1. For this example, there is no load inclination, no base inclination, and no ground inclination.
ic = 1 (Row 13)
bc = 1 (Row 14)
gc = 1 (Row 15)
Step 4a | For the USACE method, bearing capacity pressure for Layer 2 is calculated for Row 14.
qult,2 = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult,2 = 1.2 · 1.06 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.5 ksf · 5.14 + 0.27 ksf
qult,2 = 3.27 ksf + 0.27 ksf = 3.54 ksf
Step 4b | For the FHWA method, bearing capacity pressure for Layer 2 is calculated for Row 14.
qult,2 = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult,2 = 1.2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.5 ksf · 5.14 + 0.27 ksf
qult,2 = 3.08 ksf + 0.27 ksf = 3.35 ksf
[p. 309]
Step 5a | The bearing capacity at the footing level for a punch-through failure is increased due to load spreading. The ratio of qult to the calculated qult for Layer 2 (qult,2) is determined from (Eq. 5-17).
qult/(qult,2) = ((B′ + Hs) · (L′ + Hs))/(B · L) = ((7 ft + 6 ft) · (7 ft + 6 ft))/(7 ft · 7 ft) = 3.45
For the USACE method:
qult = qult/(qult,2) · qult,2 = 3.45 · 3.54 ksf = 12.21 ksf
Step 5b | For the FHWA method:
qult = qult/(qult,2) · qult,2 = 3.45 · 3.35 ksf = 11.56 ksf
Step 6 | The load on the soil is a combination of the column load and foundation weight, therefore, is expressed as a stress based on the effective area (Eq. 5-13).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′
Column load, Q = 90 kips (Row 24)
Unit weight of concrete, γconc = 0.150 kcf
Weight of foundation, Wf = A · Df · γconc = 49 ft^2 · 2 ft · 0.150 kcf = 14.7 kips (Row 25)
Gross equivalent bearing pressure, (Eq. 5-13) (Row 26).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′ = (90 kips + 14.7 kips)/(49 ft^2) = 2.14 ksf
Step 7a | The minimum factor of safety for ultimate bearing capacity is 3 (Chapter 2). For the USACE method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23) (Row 27).
FS = qult/qeq = (12.21 ksf)/(2.14 ksf) = 5.7 ≥ 3 OK ü
Step 7b | For the FHWA method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23) (Row 27).
S = qult/qeq = (11.56 ksf)/(2.14 ksf) = 5.4 ≥ 3 OK ü

[p. 309] Discussion for Example B-3. For the layered sand over clay foundation in this example, the resistance to a punch-through failure into the clay foundation was less than that for a failure in the upper sand layer. The punch-through failure will control the bearing capacity design factor of safety. The factors of safety using both the USACE and FHWA methods met the minimum requirements from Table 2-1. sections.title: Given
sections.body:
[p. 311] Given: The groundwater table is lowered from a depth of 6 to 12 ft below grade to support construction of a building. The water table will rise back to a depth of 6 ft for normal operation of the building (see Figure B-4). A 7.0-ft by 7.0-ft isolated footing supporting an 80-kip column load will bear 2 ft below the bottom of the excavation after construction and after the water has returned to a depth of 6 ft below the ground surface.

Figure B-4. Foundation and soil conditions for Example B-4

[p. 312] Table B-4a Solution for the end-of-construction phase (dewatered case)
Step 1 | Collect geometric information for the problem and input to Table B-4c. There is no eccentricity (e = 0), so footing geometry is equal to effective footing geometry (see paragraph 5-4a).
Footing width, B = B′ = 7 ft (Row 1)
Footing length, L = L′ = 7 ft (Row 2)
Footing effective area, A′ = B′ · L′ = 7 ft · 7 ft = 49 ft^2 (Row 3)
Embedment depth of the footing, Df = 2 ft (Row 4)
Unit wt. between base of the footing and ground surface, γ = 0.133 kcf (Row 5)
Step 2 | Use Eq. 5-22 for undrained qult and correction factors in Table 5-4.
Step 3 | For undrained analysis with φ = 0, Nγ is zero. The value of cohesion, c, is taken as the undrained strength su. Eq. 5-22 simplifies to qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + sq · dq · iq ·
bq · gq · q0 · Nq. Since Nq = 1 for φ = 0, and all undrained correction factors are 1 (Table 5-4), Eq. 5-29 further simplifies to:
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
The total stress at the base of the footing is:
qo = γ · Df = 0.133 kcf · 2 ft = 0.226 ksf (Row 6)
[Note (not printed): Table B-4a, Step 3 (p. 312): 0.133 kcf · 2 ft is 0.266 ksf, printed 0.226 ksf; Steps 4a and 4b (pp. 313-314) and Table B-4b carry 0.226 ksf into qult (5.78 and 5.47 ksf; with 0.266 ksf they are 5.82 and 5.51 ksf). The numbers above are as printed.]
The shear zone is typically taken as 1 footing width, or 7 ft. The bottom of the shear zone estimated as Df = B = 9 ft. If the soil in Layer 2 (10 ft to 25 ft) is weaker than soil in Layer 1 (0 ft to 10 ft), a deeper shear zone will need to be checked. The Layer 2 soil is stronger, so strength of Layer 1 soil is used for analysis.
c = su = 850 psf = 0.85 ksf (Row 7)
The cohesion bearing capacity factor Nc = 2 + π = 5.14 (Row 8)
The undrained shape factor for both the USACE and FHWA methods is (Table 5-4):
sc = 1 + 0.2 (B′/L′) = 1 + 0.2((7 ft)/(7 ft)) = 1.2 (Row 9)
The undrained depth factor for the USACE methods is (Table 5-4):
dc = 1 + 0.2 (Df/B′) ≤ 1.5 = 1 + 0.2((2 ft)/(7 ft)) = 1.06 (Row 10)
The FHWA method does not explicitly include a depth for undrained analysis, so dc = 1. For this example, there is no load inclination and no base inclination.
ic = 1 (Row 11)
bc = 1 (Row 12)
The footing is in a basement, and an upward-sloping ground surface could be considered. However, since the footing is more than 2 widths from the edge of the excavation (see Table 5-4), the overlying soil will not influence the bearing capacity response and gc can be considered as one.
gc = 1 (Row 13)
[p. 313]
Step 4a | For the USACE method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 14.
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult = 1.2 · 1.06 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.85 ksf · 5.14 + 0.226 ksf
qult = 5.56 ksf + 0.226 ksf = 5.78 ksf
Step 4b | For the FHWA method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 14.
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult = 1.2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.85 ksf · 5.14 + 0.226 ksf
qult = 5.24 ksf + 0.226 ksf = 5.47 ksf
Step 5 | The load on the soil is a combination of the column load and foundation weight and is expressed as a stress based on the effective area (Eq. 5-13).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′
Column load, Q = 80 kips (Row 15)
Unit weight of concrete, γconc = 0.150 kcf
Weight of foundation, Wf = A · Df · γconc = 49 ft^2 · 2 ft · 0.15 kcf = 14.7 kips (Row 16)
Pore pressure at base of footing with water table lowered to 12 ft during construction:
uD = 2 ft · 0.0624 kcf = 0.125 ksf
Gross equivalent bearing pressure (Eq. 5-13) (Row 17).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′ − uD = (80 kips + 14.7 kips)/(49 ft^2) − 0.125 ksf = 1.81 ksf
Step 6a | The minimum factor of safety for ultimate bearing capacity is 3 (Chapter 2). For the USACE method at the end of construction, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (5.78 ksf)/(1.81 ksf) = 3.2 ≥ 3 OK ü
Step 6b | For the FHWA method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (5.47 ksf)/(1.81 ksf) = 3.0 ≥ 3 OK ü

[p. 314] Table B-4b Solution for the long-term water level case
Step 1 | Increasing the water table level does not change the soil resistance for an undrained analysis. All values in Rows 1 through 14 are the case as for the end of construction case. For the USACE method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 14.
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult = 1.2 · 1.06 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.85 ksf · 5.14 + 0.226 ksf
qult = 5.56 ksf + 0.226 ksf = 5.78 ksf
For the FHWA method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 14.
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult = 1.2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.85 ksf · 5.14 + 0.226 ksf
qult = 5.24 ksf + 0.226 ksf = 5.47 ksf
Step 2 | The load on the soil is the same as for the end-of-construction case, and values in rows 15 and 16 are the same.
Pore pressure at base of footing changes. The height of water above the base of the footing increases from 2 ft to 8 ft:
uD = 8 ft · 0.0624 kcf = 0.499 ksf
Gross equivalent bearing pressure (Eq. 5-13) (Row 17).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′ − uD = (80 kips + 14.7 kips)/(49 ft^2) − 0.499 ksf = 1.43 ksf
Step 3a | The minimum factor of safety for ultimate bearing capacity is 3 (Chapter 2). For the USACE method at the end of construction, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (5.78 ksf)/(1.43 ksf) = 4.0 ≥ 3 OK ü
Step 3b | For the FHWA method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (5.47 ksf)/(1.43 ksf) = 3.8 ≥ 3 OK ü

sections.body:
[p. 314] Discussion for Example B-4. The undrained factors of safety using both the USACE and FHWA methods met the minimum requirements from Chapter 2 for both the end-of-construction and long-term loading case. As the water table rose, the buoyancy of the footing led to an increase in the bearing capacity safety factor. The footing meets undrained bearing capacity ultimate limit state requirements.

sections.title: Determine
sections.body: [p. 315] Determine: Calculate the factor of safety for undrained bearing capacity using both undrained strength and pressuremeter limit pressure and compare to minimum requirements to see if footing is acceptable. Evaluate potential for punch through.
sections.applicability: EM 1110-1-1905, Appendix B (Design Examples: Geotechnical Ultimate Limit States for Static Analysis), paragraph B-5a, printed p. 315.

sections.title: Given
sections.body:
[p. 315] Given: An 8-ft by 8-ft isolated footing supporting a 300-kip column load and bearing 2.5 ft below grade. Texas Rapid Assessment Method (TEXAM) PMT were conducted in clay soils as illustrated in Figure B-5. Groundwater was not encountered. The moist unit weight of the clay is 125 pcf.

[p. 316] Figure B-5. Foundation and soil conditions for Example B-5

[p. 317] Table B-5a Solution for the analysis of bearing capacity based on undrained strength
Step 1 | Collect geometric information for the problem and input to Table B-5e. There is no eccentricity (e = 0), so footing geometry is equal to effective footing geometry (see paragraph 5-4a).
Footing width, B = B′ = 8 ft (Row 1)
Footing length, L = L′ = 8 ft (Row 2)
Footing effective area, A′ = B′ · L′ = 8 ft · 8 ft = 64 ft^2 (Row 3)
Embedment depth of the footing, Df = 2.5 ft (Row 4)
Unit wt. between base of the footing and ground surface, γ = 0.125 kcf (Row 5)
Step 2 | Use Eq. 5-22 for undrained qult and correction factors in Table 5-4.
Step 3 | For undrained analysis with φ = 0, Nγ is zero. The value of cohesion, c, is taken as the undrained strength, su. Eq. 5-22 simplifies to
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq.
Since Nq = 1 for φ = 0, and all undrained correction factors are 1 (Table 5-4), Eq. 5-29 further simplifies to:
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0
The total stress at the base of the footing is:
qo = γ · Df = 0.125 kcf · 2.5 ft = 0.31 ksf (Row 6)
The shear zone is typically taken as 1 footing width, or 8 ft. The bottom of the shear zone estimated as Df + B = 10.5 ft, within the Layer 1 clay (su = 3.2 ksf). The undrained strength of 3.2 ksf will be used for these analyses. Since the soil in Layer 2 (11 ft to 17 ft) is weaker than soil in Layer 1 (0 ft to 10 ft), a deeper shear zone will also be checked in a separate punch-through analysis.
c = su = 3,200 psf = 3.2 ksf (Row 7)
The cohesion bearing capacity factor, Nc = 2 + π = 5.14 (Row 8)
The undrained shape factor for both the USACE and FHWA methods is (Table 5-4):
sc = 1 + 0.2 (B′/L′) = 1 + 0.2((8 ft)/(8 ft)) = 1.2 (Row 9)
The undrained depth factor for the USACE methods is (Table 5-4):
dc = 1 + 0.2 (Df/B′) ≤ 1.5 = 1 + 0.2 ((2.5 ft)/(8 ft)) = 1.06 (Row 10)
The FHWA method does not explicitly include a depth for undrained analysis, so dc = 1. For this example, there is no load inclination, no base inclination, and no ground inclination.
ic = 1 (Row 11)
bc = 1 (Row 12)
gc = 1 (Row 13)
[p. 318]
Step 4a | For the USACE method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 17.
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult = 1.2 · 1.06 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 3.2 ksf · 5.14 + 0.31 ksf
qult = 20.92 ksf + 0.31 ksf = 21.23 ksf
Step 4b | For the FHWA method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 17.
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult = 1.2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 3.2 ksf · 5.14 + 0.31 ksf
qult = 19.73 ksf + 0.31 ksf = 20.05 ksf
Step 5 | The load on the soil is a combination of the column load and foundation weight; it is expressed as a stress based on the effective area (Eq. 5-13).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′
Column load, Q = 300 kips (Row 15)
Unit weight of concrete, γconc = 0.150 kcf
Weight of foundation, Wf = A · Df · γconc = 64 ft^2 · 2.5 ft · 0.15 kcf = 24 kips (Row 16)
Pore pressure at base of footing, uD = 0 ksf
Gross equivalent bearing pressure, (Eq. 5-13) (Row 17).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′ − uD = (300 kips + 24 kips)/(64 ft^2) − 0 ksf = 5.06 ksf
Step 6a | The minimum factor of safety for ultimate bearing capacity is 3 (Chapter 2). For the USACE method at the end of construction, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (21.23 ksf)/(5.06 ksf) = 4.2 ≥ 3 OK ü
Step 6b | For the FHWA method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-29).
FS = qult/qeq = (20.05 ksf)/(5.06 ksf) = 4.0 ≥ 3 OK ü

[p. 319] Table B-5b Solution for the bearing capacity analysis based on the pressuremeter
Step 1 | All geometric information is the same as that for the analysis based on undrained strength. Rows 1 through 5 are the same.
Step 2 | Identify that the problem involves low permeability soils (clayey soils and plastic silts) and that the bearing capacity limit state must be assessed for undrained conditions (Table 5-1). Use Eq. 5-26 for qult and correction factors in Table 5-4.
Step 3 | All correction factors for the pressuremeter are the same as those for the USACE undrained method in Table 5-4. Rows 9 through 13 are the same as the USACE column for the undrained analysis.
Step 4 | To evaluate soil strength (s), the pressuremeter method uses the geometric mean of the net limit pressure within 1.5B of the base of the footing (Eq. 5-24). The bottom of the zone is Df + 1.5B = 2.5 ft + 1.5(8 ft) = 14.5 ft. The zone for soil strength assessment includes the three measurements in the overlying strong layer and two measurements in the underlying weaker layer (Row 9).
s = pne = ʸ√(pn1 · pn2 · ⋯pny) = ⁵√(28 ksf · 33 ksf · 39.6 ksf · 4.4 ksf · 6.2 ksf) = 15.8 ksf
Step 5 | For undrained pressuremeter bearing capacity analysis, (Eq. 5-26)
qult = k · sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · s + q0 = k · sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · pne + q0
qo = γ · Df = 0.125 kcf · 2.5 ft = 0.31 (Row 6).
The pressuremeter k-factor for continuous footings is 0.7 (Table 5-5) (Row 8)
qult = 0.7 · 1.2 · 1.06 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 15.8 ksf + 0.31 ksf
qult = 14.07 ksf + 0.31 ksf = 14.38 ksf
Step 6 | The load on the soil is the same as the analysis based on undrained strength. Rows 18 through 21 are the same.
Step 7 | The minimum factor of safety for ultimate bearing capacity is 3 (Chapter 2). For the pressuremeter method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (14.38 ksf)/(5.06 ksf) = 2.8 ≤ 3 NOT OK û

[p. 320] Table B-5c Solution for punch-through analysis based on undrained strength
Step 1 | All geometric information is the same as that for the analysis based on undrained strength. Rows 1 through 5 are the same.
Step 2 | Identify that the problem involves low permeability soils (clayey soils and plastic silts) and that the bearing capacity limit state must be assessed for undrained conditions (Table 5-1). Use Eq. 5-22 for qult and correction factors in Table 5-4.
Step 3 | All correction factors for the punch-through analysis are the same as those for the undrained method. Rows 8 through 13 are the same as the USACE column for the undrained analysis.
Step 4 | The punch-through analysis assumes a failure in Layer 2, with an undrained strength of 600 psf = 0.6 ksf (Row 7).
Step 5a | For the USACE method, the punch-through bearing capacity for Layer 2 is calculated in Row 14.
qult,2 = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult,2 = 1.2 · 1.06 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.6 ksf · 5.14 + 0.31 ksf
qult,2 = 3.92 ksf + 0.31 ksf = 4.23 ksf
Step 5b | For the FHWA method, the punch-through bearing capacity for Layer 2 is calculated in Row 14.
qult,2 = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult,2 = 1.2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.6 ksf · 5.14 + 0.31 ksf
qult,2 = 3.70 ksf + 0.31 ksf = 4.01 ksf
Step 6 | The bearing capacity at the footing level for a punch-through failure is increased due to load spreading. The ratio of qult to the calculated qult for Layer 2 (qult,2) is determined from (Eq. 5-17).
qult/(qult,2) = ((B′ + Hs) · (L′ + Hs))/(B · L) = ((8 ft + 8.5 ft) · (8 ft + 8.5 ft))/(8 ft · 8 ft) = 4.25
For the USACE method:
qult = qult/(qult,2) · qult,2 = 4.25 · 4.23 ksf = 17.98 ksf
For the FHWA method:
qult = qult/(qult,2) · qult,2 = 4.25 · 4.01 ksf = 17.04 ksf
Step 7 | The load on the soil is the same as the analysis based on undrained strength. Rows 18 through 21 are the same.
Step 8a | The minimum factor of safety for ultimate bearing capacity is 3 (Chapter 2). For the USACE method at the end of construction, the factor of safety was calculated as
(Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (17.98 ksf)/(5.06 ksf) = 3.6 ≥ 3 OK ü
[p. 321]
Step 8b | For the FHWA method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23).
FS = qult/qeq = (17.04 ksf)/(5.06 ksf) = 3.4 ≥ 3 OK ü

Table B-5d Average safety factor from multiple methods
For undrained strength-based analysis, the punch-through failure provided a lower factor of safety. The factors of safety for failure in the overlying strong layer are irrelevant, and not included in the final assessment. Undrained strength-based factors of safety are:
USACE FS = 3.6
FHWA FS = 3.4
The factor of safety based on pressuremeter analysis is more conservative since it does not explicitly consider the punch-through failure mechanism. PMT FS = 2.8
Section 5-5f recommends averaging the results of analyses performed when determining a design safety factor.
FS = (3.6 + 3.4 + 2.8)/3 = 9.9/3 = 3.3 ≥ 3 OK ü

sections.title: Discussion for Example B-5
sections.body:
[p. 321] Discussion for Example B-5. The factors of safety using both the USACE and FHWA methods met the minimum requirements from Table 2-1. The punch-through failure mechanism gave a lower FS and was more critical. While the PMT method includes strength from the underlying weak layer in limit pressure averaging, it does not explicitly account for differences in the mechanism itself. The differences between the PMT and undrained strength mechanism indicate some additional uncertainty in results, however, the average factor of safety for the three methods was greater than 3. The footing meets undrained bearing capacity ultimate limit state requirements.

sections.title: Determine
sections.body: [p. 322] Determine: Calculate the drained vertical bearing capacity for an isolated footing on sand with water table in the shear zone (as compared to undrained punch-through failure into soft clay). Calculate the factor of safety for bearing capacity and compare to minimum requirements to see if footing is acceptable.
sections.applicability: EM 1110-1-1905, Appendix B (Design Examples: Geotechnical Ultimate Limit States for Static Analysis), paragraph B-6a, printed p. 322.

sections.title: Given
sections.body:
[p. 323] Given: An 8-ft by 8-ft isolated footing supporting a 300-kip column load bears 2.5 ft below existing grade. Reference the mixed soil profile in Figure B-6. The moist unit weight for the clay and sand is 120 pcf.

Figure B-6. Foundation and soil conditions for Example B-6

Table B-6a Solution for drained bearing capacity analysis within surface layer
Step 1 | Collect geometric information for the problem and input to Table B-6c. There is no eccentricity (e = 0), so footing geometry is equal to effective footing geometry (see paragraph 5-4a).
Footing width, B = B′ = 8 ft (Row 1)
Footing length, L = L′ = 8 ft (Row 2)
Footing effective Area, A′ = B′ · L′ = 8 ft · 8 ft = 64 ft^2 (Row 3)
Embedment depth of the footing, Df = 2.5 ft (Row 4)
Depth of water table, Dw = 8 ft (Row 5)
Unit wt. between base of the footing and ground surface, γ = 0.120 kcf (Row 6)
[p. 324]
Step 2 | Identify that the problem involves free-draining soils (sands, silty sands, and non-plastic silts) in the layer immediately below the footing and that the bearing capacity limit state must be assessed for drained conditions (Table 5-1). Use Eq. 5-22 for qult and correction factors in Table 5-2 and Table 5-3.
Step 3 | For drained analysis with cohesion c = 0, Eq. 5-22 simplifies to
qult = sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq + sγ · dγ · iγ · bγ · gγ · 1/2 · B′ · γ′ · Nγ
The ratio of the effective unit weight in the shear zone to the total unit weight differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE (Eq. 5-19) (Row 7):
γ′/γ ≈ [0.45 + 0.55 ((max(DW − Df, 0))/B)] ≤ 1
γ′/γ ≈ [0.45 + 0.55 ((max(8 ft − 2.5 ft, 0))/(8 ft))] ≤ 1 = 0.45 + 0.55 · 0.69 = 0.83
For FHWA (Eq. 5-20) (Row 7):
γ′/γ ≈ CWγ = [0.5 + 0.5 (DW/(1.5B + Df))] ≤ 1
γ′/γ ≈ CWγ = [0.5 + 0.5 ((8 ft)/(1.5(8 ft) + 2.5 ft))] ≤ 1 = 0.5 + 0.5 · 0.55 = 0.78
The effective stress at the base of the footing is:
qo = γ · Df − uD = 0.12 kcf · 2.5 ft − 0 ksf = 0.3 ksf (Row 8)
The shear zone is typically taken as 1 footing width, or 8 ft. The bottom of the shear zone estimated as Df + B = 10.5 ft. The estimated shear zone is within Layer 1 (0 ft to 15.5 ft), so strength of Layer 1 soil is used for analysis. Punch-through failure into the underlying weak layer will be checked in a separate analysis.
φ′ = 31° (Row 9)
The flow number, or principal stress ratio, is (Table 5-2) (Row 10):
N = (1 + sinφ′)/(1 − sinφ′) = (1 + sin(31°))/(1 − sin(31°)) = 1.515/0.485 = 3.12
[p. 325]
Step 4 | The dimensionless bearing capacity for surcharge is (Table 5-2) (Row 11):
Nq = N · e^(π·tanφ′) = 3.12e^(π·tan(31°)) = 3.12e^1.89 = 3.12 · 6.62 = 20.6
The drained shape factor for surcharge differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE (Table 5-2) (Row 12):
sq = 1 + 0.1N(B′/L′) = 1 + 0.1 · 3.12 ((8 ft)/(8 ft)) = 1.31
For FHWA (Table 5-2) (Row 12):
sq = 1 + [(B′/L′) tanφ] = 1 + [((8 ft)/(8 ft)) tan(31°)] = 1 + (1 · 0.6) = 1.6
The drained depth factor for surcharge differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, (Table 5-2) (Row 13):
dq = 1 + 0.1√N(Df/B′) = 1 + 0.1√3.12 ((2.5 ft)/(8 ft)) = 1 + 0.1 · 1.77 · 0.31 = 1.06
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 13):
dq = 1 + 2 · tanφ′ · (1 − sinφ′)^2 · atan(Df/B′)
dq = 1 + 2 · tan(31°) · (1 − sin(31°))^2 · atan((2.5 ft)/(8 ft))
dq = 1 + 2 · 0.6 · (1 − 0.515)^2 · 0.30 = 1.09
For this example, there is no load inclination, no base inclination, and no ground inclination.
ic = 1 (Row 14)
bc = 1 (Row 15)
gc = 1 (Row 16)
Step 5 | The dimensionless bearing capacity for soil effective weight differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, (Table 5-2) (Row 17):
Nγ = (Nq − 1) · tan(1.4φ′) = (29.46 − 1) · tan(1.4 · 31°)
[Note (not printed): Table B-6a, Step 4 (p. 325): the USACE Nγ line prints (29.46 − 1), Example B-3's Nq (p. 306); this example's Nq is 20.6 (Row 12), and the next line uses 20.6 − 1 = 19.6. The line above is as printed.]
Nγ = 19.6 · tan(43.4°) = 19.6 · 0.945 = 18.5
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 17):
Nγ = 2(Nq + 1) · tan(φ′) = 2 · (20.6 + 1) · tan(31°)
Nγ = 43.2 · 0.6 = 26
The drained shape factor for soil effective weight differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, the shape factors for surcharge and soil effective weight are the same (Table 5-2) (Row 18):
sγ = 1 + 0.1N (B′/L′) = 1 + 0.1 · 3.12 · (8 ft)/(8 ft) = 1.31
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 18):
sγ = 1 − 0.4 (B′/L′) = 1 − 0.4 ((8 ft)/(8 ft)) = 1 − 0.4 = 0.6
[p. 326]
 | The drained depth factor for surcharge soil effective weight differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, the shape factors for surcharge and soil effective weight are the same (Table 5-2) (Row 19):
dγ = 1 + 0.1√N(Df/B′) = 1 + 0.1√3.12 ((2.5 ft)/(8 ft)) = 1 + 0.1 · 1.77 · 0.31 = 1.06
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 19): dγ = 1
For this example, there is no load inclination, no base inclination, and no ground inclination.
ic = 1 (Row 20)
bc = 1 (Row 21)
gc = 1 (Row 22)
Step 6a | For the USACE method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 23 as:
qult = sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq + sγ · dγ · iγ · bγ · gγ · 1/2 · B′ · γ′ · Nγ
qult = 1.31 · 1.06 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.3 ksf · 20.6 + 1.31 · 1.06 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1/2 · 8 ft · 0.83 · 0.12 kcf · 18.5
qult = 8.58 ksf + 10.23 ksf = 18.8 ksf
Step 6b | For the FHWA method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 23 as:
qult = sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq + sγ · dγ · iγ · bγ · gγ · 1/2 · B′ · γ′ · Nγ
qult = 1.6 · 1.09 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.3 ksf · 20.6 + 0.6 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1/2 · 8 ft · 0.78 · 0.12 kcf · 26
qult = 10.78 ksf + 5.85 ksf = 16.6 ksf
Step 7 | The load on the soil is a combination of the column load and foundation weight and is expressed as a stress based on the effective area (Eq. 5-13).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′
Column load, Q = 300 kips (Row 24)
Unit weight of concrete, γconc = 0.150 kcf
Weight of foundation, Wf = A · Df · γconc = 64 ft^2 · 2.5 ft · 0.15 kcf = 24 kips (Row 25)
Gross equivalent bearing pressure, (Eq. 5-13) (Row 26).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′ − uD = (300 kips + 24 kips)/(64 ft^2) − 0 ksf = 5.06 ksf
Step 8a | The minimum factor of safety for ultimate bearing capacity is 3 (Chapter 2). For the USACE method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23) (Row 27).
FS = qult/qeq = (18.8 ksf)/(5.06 ksf) = 3.7 ≥ 3 OK ü
Step 8b | For the FHWA method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23) (Row 27).
FS = qult/qeq = (16.6 ksf)/(5.06 ksf) = 3.3 ≥ 3 OK ü

[p. 327] Table B-6b Solution for undrained punch-through analysis
Step 1 | Collect geometric information for the problem and input to Table B-6c. There is no eccentricity (e = 0), so footing geometry is equal to effective footing geometry (see paragraph 5-4a). The geometry information is the same as that for the drained analysis of Layer 1.
Footing width, B = B′ = 8 ft (Row 1)
Footing length, L = L′ = 8 ft (Row 2)
Footing effective area, A′ = B′ · L′ = 8 ft · 8 ft = 64 ft^2 (Row 3)
Embedment depth of the footing, Df = 2.5 ft (Row 4)
Depth of water table, Dw = 8 ft (Row 5)
Unit wt. between base of the footing and ground surface, γ = 0.120 kcf (Row 6)
Step 2 | Identify that the problem of punch-through into the underlying soil involves low permeability soils (clayey soils and plastic silts) and that the bearing capacity limit state must be assessed for undrained conditions (Table 5-1). Use Eq 5-22 for qult and correction factors in Table 5-4.
Step 3 | For undrained analysis with φ = 0, Nγ is zero. The value of cohesion, c, is taken as the undrained strength su. Eq. 5-22 simplifies to qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + sq · dq · iq ·
bq · gq · q0 · Nq. Since Nq = 1 for φ = 0, and all undrained correction factors are 1 (Table 5-4), Eq. 5-29 further simplifies to:
qult = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
The total stress at the base of the footing is:
qo = γ · Df = 0.12 kcf · 2.5 ft = 0.3 ksf (Row 8)
The shear zone is typically taken as 1 footing width, or 7 ft, but may extend to approximately 2 footings widths when softer soils are at depth. The weaker soils in Layer 2 soil are used for the punch-through analysis.
c = su = 400 psf = 0.4 ksf (Row 9)
The cohesion bearing capacity factor Nc = 2π = 5.14 (Row 10)
The undrained shape factor for both the USACE and FHWA methods is (Table 5-4):
sc = 1 + 0.2 (B′/L′) = 1 + 0.2((8 ft)/(8 ft)) = 1.2 (Row 11)
The undrained depth factor for the USACE methods is (Table 5-4):
dc = 1 + 0.2 (Df/B′) ≤ 1.5 = 1 + 0.2((2.5 ft)/(8 ft)) = 1.06 (Row 12)
The FHWA method does not explicitly include a depth for undrained analysis, so dc = 1. For this example, there is no load inclination, no base inclination, and no ground inclination.
ic = 1 (Row 13)
bc = 1 (Row 14)
gc = 1 (Row 15)
[p. 328]
Step 4a | For the USACE method, bearing capacity pressure for Layer 2 is calculated for Row 16.
qult,2 = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult,2 = 1.2 · 1.06 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.4 ksf · 5.14 + 0.3 ksf
qult,2 = 2.62 ksf + 0.3 ksf = 2.92 ksf
Step 4b | For the FHWA method, bearing capacity pressure for Layer 2 is calculated for Row 16.
qult,2 = sc · dc · ic · bc · gc · su · Nc + q0.
qult,2 = 1.2 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 1 · 0.4 ksf · 5.14 + 0.3 ksf
qult,2 = 2.47 ksf + 0.3 ksf = 2.77 ksf
Step 5 | The bearing capacity at the footing level for a punch-through failure is increased due to load spreading. The ratio of qult to the calculated qult for Layer 2 (qult,2) is determined from (Eq. 5-17). (Row 18)
qult/(qult,2) = ((B′ + Hs) · (L′ + Hs))/(B · L) = ((8 ft + 13 ft) · (8 ft + 13 ft))/(8 ft · 8 ft) = 6.89
For the USACE method, (Row 23):
qult = qult/(qult,2) · qult,2 = 6.89 · 2.92 ksf = 20.1 ksf
For the FHWA method, (Row 23):
qult = qult/(qult,2) · qult,2 = 6.89 · 2.77 ksf = 19.1 ksf
Step 6 | The load on the soil is the same as the analysis based on undrained strength. Rows 24 through 27 are the same.
Step 7a | The minimum factor of safety for ultimate bearing capacity is 3 (Chapter 2). For the USACE method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23) (Row 27).
FS = qult/qeq = (20.1 ksf)/(5.06 ksf) = 4 ≥ 3 OK ü
Step 7b | For the FHWA method, the factor of safety was calculated as (Eq. 5-23) (Row 27).
FS = qult/qeq = (19.1 ksf)/(5.06 ksf) = 3.8 ≥ 3 OK ü

sections.title: Discussion for Example B-6
sections.body:
[p. 328] Discussion for Example B-6. For the layered sand over clay foundation in this example, a punch-through failure into the clay foundation provided less resistance than that for a failure in the upper sand layer. The punch-through failure will control the design factor of safety. The factors of safety using both the USACE and FHWA methods met the minimum requirements from Chapter 2. The footing meets bearing capacity ultimate limit state requirements.
[Note (not printed): Discussion for Example B-6 (p. 328) and Table B-6b, Step 5 (p. 327): Table B-6c (p. 329) prints qult = 18.82 ksf (USACE) and 16.62 ksf (FHWA) for failure in the sand layer and 20.12 and 19.09 ksf for punch-through, so the punch-through values are the larger. Eq. 5-17 (p. 102) takes the lesser, qult = min(qult,1, spreading factor · qult,2): 18.82 ksf (USACE) and 16.62 ksf (FHWA), the sand layer, with FS = 3.7 and 3.3 (Table B-6a, Step 8; Row 28), both at least 3. The words above are as printed.]

sections.title: Determine
sections.body: [p. 330] Determine: Calculate the drained bearing capacity in sand. Compare soil parameters with in situ tests. Calculate the factor of safety for bearing capacity and compare to minimum requirements to see if footing is acceptable. Use methods based on friction angle, SPT, CPT, and PMT.
sections.applicability: EM 1110-1-1905, Appendix B (Design Examples: Geotechnical Ultimate Limit States for Static Analysis), paragraph B-7a, printed p. 330.

sections.title: Given
sections.body:
[p. 330] Given: An 8-ft by 8-ft isolated footing supporting a 400-kip column load bears 2.5 ft below existing grade as illustrated in Figure B-7. TEXAM PMT, CPT, and SPT were conducted on sandy soils as illustrated in Figure B-7. The moist unit weight of the sand is 125 pcf. Groundwater was not encountered.

Figure B-7. Foundation and soil conditions for Example B-7

Table B-7a Solution for drained bearing capacity analysis within surface layer
Step 1 | Collect geometric information for the problem. There is no eccentricity (e = 0), so footing geometry is equal to effective footing geometry (see paragraph 5-4a).
Footing width, B = B′ = 8 ft (Row 1)
Footing length, L = L′ = 8 ft (Row 2)
Footing effective area, A′ = B′ · L′ = 8 ft · 8 ft = 64 ft^2 (Row 3)
Embedment depth of the footing, Df = 2.5 ft (Row 4)
Depth of water table, Dw = not encountered (effective stress = total stress)
Unit wt. between base of the footing and ground surface, γ = 0.125 kcf (Row 6)
[p. 331]
Step 2 | Identify that the problem involves free-draining soils (sands, silty sands, and non-plastic silts) in the layer immediately below the footing and that the bearing capacity limit state must be assessed for drained conditions (Table 5-1). Use Eq. 5-22 for qult and correction factors in Table 5-2 and Table 5-3.
Step 3 | For drained analysis with c = 0, Eq. 5-22 simplifies to:
qult = sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq + sγ · dγ · iγ · bγ · gγ · 1/2 · B′ · γ′ · Nγ
Water was not encountered within the upper 20 ft. When water is not expected for critical load cases, the total stress is equal to the effective stress and total unit weight is used for calculations (γ′/γ = 1) for both USACE and FHWA methods (Row 7).
The effective stress at the base of the footing is:
qo = γ · Df − uo = 0.125 kcf · 2.5 ft − 0 ksf = 0.31 ksf (Row 8)
The shear zone is typically taken as 1 footing width, or 8 ft. The bottom of the shear zone estimated as Df + B = 10.5 ft. Since the soil are denser below 7.5 ft, it is assumed that the shear zone is isolated in the weaker layer with φ′ = 32°.
φ′ = 32° (Row 9)
The flow number, or principal stress ratio, is (Table 5-2) (Row 10):
N = (1 + sinφ′)/(1 − sinφ′) = (1 + sin(32°))/(1 − sin(32°)) = 1.53/0.47 = 3.26
[p. 332]
Step 4 | The dimensionless bearing capacity for surcharge is (Table 5-2) (Row 11):
Nq = N · e^(π·tanφ′) = 3.26e^(π·tan(32°)) = 3.26e^1.96 = 3.26 · 7.1 = 23.1
The drained shape factor for surcharge differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, (Table 5-2) (Row 12):
sq = 1 + 0.1N(B′/L′) = 1 + 0.1 · 3.26 ((8 ft)/(8 ft)) = 1.33
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 12):
sq = 1 + (B′/L′) tanφ = 1 + ((8 ft)/(8 ft)) tan(32°) = 1 + (1 · 0.62) = 1.62
The drained depth factor for surcharge differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, (Table 5-2) (Row 13):
dq = 1 + 0.1√N(Df/B′) = 1 + 0.1√3.26 ((2.5 ft)/(8 ft)) = 1 + 0.1 · 1.81 · 0.31 = 1.06
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 13):
dq = 1 + 2 · tanφ′ · (1 − sinφ′)^2 · atan(Df/B′)
dq = 1 + 2 · tan(32°) · (1 − sin(32°))^2 · atan((2.5 ft)/(8 ft))
dq = 1 + 2 · 0.62(1 − 0.53)^2 · 0.30 = 1.08
For this example, there is no load inclination, no base inclination, and no ground inclination.
ic = 1 (Row 14)
bc = 1 (Row 15)
gc = 1 (Row 16)
[p. 333]
Step 5 | The dimensionless bearing capacity for soil effective weight differs for the USACE and FHWA methods. For USACE, (Table 5-2) (Row 17):
Nγ = (Nq − 1) · tan(1.4φ′) = (23.1 − 1) · tan(1.4 · 32°)
Nγ = 22.1 · tan(44.8°) = 22.1 · 0.99 = 21.9
For FHWA, (Table 5-2) (Row 17):

Step 6a | For the USACE method, bearing capacity pressure is calculated for Row 23 as:
qult = sq · dq · iq · bq · gq · q0 · Nq + sγ · dγ · iγ · bγ · gγ · 1/2 · B′ · γ′ · Nγ

qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′
Column Load, Q = 400 kips (Row 24)
Unit weight of concrete, γconc = 0.150 kcf
Weight of foundation, Wf = A · Df · γconc = 64 ft^2 · 2.5 ft · 0.15 kcf = 24 kips (Row 2)
Gross equivalent bearing pressure, (Eq. 5-13) (Row 26).
qeq = (Q + Wf)/A′ − uD = (400 kips + 24 kips)/(64 ft^2) − 0 ksf = 6.63 ksf

Step 2 | Identify that the problem involves free-draining soils (sands, silty sands, and non-plastic silts) in the layer immediately below the footing and that the bearing capacity limit state must be assessed for drained conditions (Table 5-1). Use Eq. 5-25 for qult and correction factors in Table 5-2 and Table 5-3.
Step 3 | All correction factors for the in situ tests are the same as those for the USACE method in Table 5-2 and Table 5-3. However, the flow number, N = 3 (Row 10) is assumed. The drained shape factor for surcharge differs for the USACE and FHWA methods.

For the pressuremeter, the shear zone has one pn measurement of 17 ksf (Row 9).
s = pne = ʸ√(pn1 · pn2 · ⋯pny) = ¹√(17 ksf) = 17 ksf
